title: The Principle of Superposition in Quantum Mechanics
text:
Quantum mechanics posits that a subatomic particle exists in a superposition of states until it is measured. This means the particle does not possess a single, definite property (such as spin or location) but rather occupies all potential states simultaneously, represented by a wave function.

The act of measurement causes the wave function to collapse, forcing the particle into one specific, observable state. The precise mechanism governing this 'collapse' remains one of the most profound and debated subjects in modern physics, giving rise to the measurement problem.

Understanding superposition is fundamental to quantum computation, where qubits leverage this principle to perform calculations vastly more complex than classical bits.
